title: Live slice switchover guardrails with synthetic probe gating and state reconciliation
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Build an orchestrator sub-controller and runbook to perform live 'slice' switchover of the private data-plane/runtime with zero-downtime guarantees and fast, deterministic rollback. This work targets VPC/private deployments where tenant slices (slot groups) are migrated between runtime versions or capacity pools with strict session and cache consistency requirements. The controller will be conservative by default and expose configurable safety thresholds for tenants with stricter SLAs.

Scope and key behaviors:
- Staged switchover model: drain -> migrate -> validate -> ramp traffic. Each stage is gated by synthetic probe results and state-reconciliation checks.
- Synthetic probe gating: run short-lived synthetic traffic to exercise common request shapes and edge cases (long-context, streaming, tool calls). Evaluate p50/p95 latency, token throughput, error rate, and determinism regression against baseline before advancing.
- State reconciliation: verify ephemeral state (in-memory caches, KV prefix snapshots, session affinity tables) is consistent post-migration. Use checksums and snapshot diffs to detect missing entries or evicted prefixes beyond acceptable thresholds.
- Priming and pre-warm: optionally pre-warm KV/cache with hotspots derived from recent traffic windows for tenants flagged as latency-sensitive. Provide metrics to validate priming hit-rate before traffic ramp.
- Traffic shaping: implement fraction-based traffic ramps (e.g., 5%, 25%, 60%, 100%) with configurable steady-state windows and automatic rollback triggers. Support both route-level and tenant-slice routing.
- Rollback policy: immediate rollback on critical regression signals (error-rate > threshold, p95 latency spike beyond threshold, kv-sync-lag > threshold) or manual rollback via console/CLI. Rollback must restore previous runtime slots and re-evaluate state to avoid flapping.
- Observability and diagnostics: emit staged events, synthetic probe results, reconciliation diffs, and pre/post-exported metrics to Console and external observability (Grafana/Datadog). Tag all metrics with tenant_id, slice_id, and upgrade_id.
- IaC hooks: expose Terraform lifecycle hooks (pre-upgrade validation and post-upgrade confirmation) for Private customers running upgrades via Terraform. Provide module examples and upgrade-timeout guardrails.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Controller can complete a staged switchover in a dev VPC with synthetic probe gating and no user-facing errors for benign migrations.
2) Automatic rollback triggers correctly detect injected regressions in canary and revert to previous slots within target RTO (5 minutes).
3) Reconciliation reports show <0.1% acceptable KV divergence for non-evicted keys in test workloads; alerts when exceeded.
4) Terraform examples and a runbook are published with clear commands to opt-in/opt-out to staged switchover.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include cross-region multi-tenant rebalancing (future work).
- Does not implement new KMS integrations.

Open design decisions:
- Quorum logic for state validation: majority of probe agents vs strict all-agents pass. (Design meeting 2026-02-25 to decide quorum.)
- Default traffic ramp cadence vs per-tenant override.

Notes for implementers:
- Use existing runtime health hooks (agent /healthz and /kv-sync) and add a lightweight reconciliation API on the runtime to export snapshots safely for comparison.
- Keep probe traffic CIDR-restricted and authenticated to avoid customer billing noise.
- Make probe definitions reusable; expose a YAML probe manifest in the operator config.

Runbook (high level):
1) Start staged switchover for slice X via CLI or Console.
2) Controller runs pre-checks and synthetic probes against baseline.
3) If pre-checks pass, controller drains connections from source slots.
4) Controller brings up target slots, streams state, runs reconciliation; runs warmup probes.
5) Ramp traffic in configured steps, monitoring thresholds at each step.
6) If any critical threshold trips, controller triggers rollback and notifies on-call with diagnostic bundle.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: State divergence causing session failures. Mitigation: conservative default to keep sessions pinned until reconciliation completes; allow per-tenant force-migration with audit.
- Risk: Probe false positives. Mitigation: use multi-metric gating and require sustained violation window.

Deliverables:
- Orchestrator controller implementation (Go) with unit/integration tests.
- Probe manifest and synthetic probe runner service.
- Terraform module examples with lifecycle hooks and docs.
- Console rollouts UI extension hooks to visualize staged progress and enable manual rollback.
- Runbook and postmortem template.
